newsitem.title: USA: Russian woman has emotional return to U.S..
newsitem.headline: Russian woman has emotional return to U.S..

text.p: A Russian woman had an emotional reunion with her family in California on Friday when she was allowed to return to the United States three months after being forced to leave by immigration authorities.

"I'm very lucky," a smiling Laura Tedeeva Korewicki said as she hugged her family and friends at San Francisco International Airport after flying in from Moscow. Saying she was happy and tired, Korewicki said she wanted to be with her friends and her husband.
The airport arrivals area was filled with whistling and applause as Korewicki was greeted by husband Andre, daughter Nana, 16, and stepdaughters Kasia, 12, and Natalia, 9.

U.S. Senator Dianne Feinstein, a Democrat, and Congressman Bill Baker, a Republican, had taken up Korewicki's cause after she was forced to leave the United States in July after a highly publicised dispute with immigration authorities, separating her from her family in California.

Korewicki, 38, came to the United States in 1992, where she sought political asylum and married. She voluntarily left the country on July 19 to avoid a formal deportation after her application for asylum was denied. Immigration authorities said she missed an asylum hearing.

Korewicki spent most of the three months since leaving the United States in Poland with her mother-in-law. She returned to Moscow recently for a hearing at the U.S. Embassy. Soon afterward U.S. authorities granted her a permanent visa.
Deportees usually cannot legally return to the United States for five years, but the State Department allowed her to return after 90 days.
After the emotional airport reunion Korewicki returned to her home in Walnut Creek, near San Francisco, for a party.
